description: A diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that inspects the actual trained recommender through a stable SASRec-compatible interface. It returns diagnostic metrics and their definitions while respecting the benchmark’s data and evaluation constraints.
motivation: Support model diagnosis and iterative improvement without fabricating unavailable attributes, accessing hidden test data, or changing the common evaluation protocol.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader). Use view.model as the trained nn.Module and adapt probes to architecture changes through item_emb, log2feats, and predict_score. Training batches contain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors shaped B × L. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; treat review content, ratings, commercial attributes, and simulator traits as unavailable. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for 20 real training users, five per category. Select models using macro-average validation HR@10 across all four categories under the pinned evaluator.
pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    init(view, device):
        retain view and device

    run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        preserve model training state
        set view.model to evaluation mode
        disable gradients
        inspect batches using architecture-compatible probes
        compute supported diagnostics from observed data
        mark unsupported diagnostics as unavailable
        restore model training state
        return metrics, metric_definitions

For simulator input:
    recommend from the full catalog excluding observed items
    use five real training users per category

For model selection:
    use pinned macro-average validation HR@10

originality.positive: Combines a stable diagnostic interface with explicit observability constraints and a shared recommendation benchmark.
originality.negative: Describes an integration contract rather than a new recommendation algorithm or diagnostic method.

future_potential.positive: Can support comparable diagnostics across architectures and guide subsequent model improvements.
future_potential.negative: Its usefulness depends on implementing informative probes; the description provides no evidence of improved recommendation accuracy.

code_difficulty.positive: The required interface, batch shapes, available inputs, and selection metric are clearly specified.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require careful probe adaptation, and full-catalog recommendation must handle masking and computational cost.
